newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit weakens as Singapore dollar rises.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit weakens as Singapore dollar rises.

text.p: The rise of the Singapore dollar pressured the ringgit lower against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
Comments by Singapore's Finance Minister Richard Hu that the Sing could be expected to maintain its more modest rise led to buying of the Sing/ringgit cross, they said.
A joint statement by Singapore and Brunei that they had no intention of ending their currency interchangeability agreement, also pushed up the Sing against the dollar and ringgit.
"Dollar/Sing selling was started by Richard Hu. Then dollar went down again on the Brunei story," said a currency analyst.
Short positions on Sing/ringgit were trimmed, pushing the Singapore unit up to 1.7231/50 ringgit at the end of Kuala Lumpur trading at 1000 GMT, from 1.7136/54 last Friday.
The ringgit was also at 2.4795/05 a dollar against 2.4785/95 on Friday.
Dealers said the ringgit may fall further against the dollar in European/U.S. trading later on Monday.
If the dollar's resistance at 2.4830 ringgit is broken, it could move higher to 2.4860, the analyst said.
